summary: Observation of the silent, arabesque movement of colored lights.
description: On December 26, 1976, at approximately 8:15 PM, two witnesses observed several minutes of pale red and yellow lights coming from the west. The lights traced arabesques as they moved slowly eastward. This phenomenon occurred above Mont Fevrier, not far from the radio station. The witnesses also saw a red sphere rise from the high-voltage power line, move toward the lights, and then disappear. No other reports were collected, and the radio station operator in Cuisseaux noticed nothing. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of seven luminous flying objects. Some move in an oscillating motion before disappearing.
description: On December 24, 1976, at approximately 7:15 PM, two witnesses observed the successive appearance of bright lights in the sky. No sound was heard during the movement of these seven lights in total. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack further details.

summary: Probable sighting of a helicopter type aircraft.
description: On December 23, 1976, at approximately 2:20 a.m., a soldier on observation duty noticed a round object flying at low altitude. The object was illuminated by several bright red lights. Another red light at its top rotated like a flashing beacon. The craft moved slowly and emitted a continuous, moderately loud whistling sound. It then disappeared, hidden behind another building. The observation lasted 30 seconds. No other direct witnesses to the sighting came forward. The soldier likely observed a helicopter.

summary: Probable astronomical observations of Sirius.
description: A witness reported an observation made on December 21, 1976, between 10:30 PM and 11:45 PM: the witness observed a luminous phenomenon of several colors using binoculars. Two other people also observed the phenomenon, which appeared stationary. These individuals likely made an astronomical observation of Sirius, which was perfectly visible at that time of year. The colors noticed by the main witness were probably the result of, on the one hand, the star's twinkling due to atmospheric disturbances, and on the other hand, chromatic aberrations inherent in consumer binoculars (these aberrations cause iridescence around very bright points).

summary: Observation of a red glow and the passage of a dark mass.
description: On December 18, 1976, at 5:00 a.m., a witness observed a red glow and a dark mass moving north-south at low altitude through their bedroom window. No noise was heard during the observation on that slightly hazy morning. No other reports were collected regarding this sighting, for which we lack further information.

summary: Observation of a weather balloon.
description: On Tuesday, December 14, 1976, between 1:15 and 1:27 a.m., a motorist noticed an unusual glow above the airport. An intensely white sphere moved laterally and slowly, followed by a second. They initially stopped before rising rapidly and disappearing. The police investigation determined that this person had witnessed the release of a weather balloon: all their observations perfectly described the balloon's maneuvers.

summary: Observations of the passage of luminous phenomena.
description: On December 10, 1976, at 10:10 PM, a witness observed an east-northwest passage of a luminous point moving silently at a speed equivalent to that of a shooting star. Ovoid in shape and silvery in color, the phenomenon left no luminous trail. Visible for a few seconds, it disappeared, hidden by the landscape. On December 11, at 1:00 AM, a member of the military observed a north-south passage of an ovoid object at high altitude, leaving a luminous trail, for 3 to 4 minutes. It is highly probable that these witnesses observed atmospheric re-entries.

summary: Observation of the presence of a significant glow in the sky followed by its high-speed movement.
description: On December 9, 1976, a couple out for a walk noticed a bright, white, stationary light in the sky. They were quite astonished by the variations in its brightness and then by its rapid and silent movement toward the southeast. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the presence and slow movement of flying objects in the valley. No noise heard. Lack of information.
description: On the nights of December 8th and 9th, 1976, around 11:00 PM, soldiers observed several unidentified, round flying objects in the sky for a few seconds. These objects moved slowly and silently from the southeast to the northwest. About ten kilometers away, a dog unit noted that on the same nights, their ten dogs had been howling unusually loudly. Another witness reported an observation made six weeks earlier: a witness saw a red light rising into the sky at the foot of the ridges before disappearing behind a peak. Following the soldiers' report, a surveillance operation was established from December 12th to 30th, but no further sightings were reported.

summary: Observations of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On December 7, 1976, at approximately 5:45 PM, a bus driver and several schoolchildren twice observed a bright, spherical object moving in the sky. The object, very bright above the sea, moved slowly towards Earth before disappearing. One hypothesis considered was that it was an astronomical object. However, no further precise information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Astronomical observations of Venus.
description: On December 1, 1976, several witnesses observed a luminous, stationary object above the horizon. The observation lasted 15 minutes before the object disappeared. No unusual noise was heard. The gendarmerie quickly arrived at the scene but made no observations, and no unusual traces were found on the ground in the area that evening. The gendarmerie investigation determined that a luminous phenomenon had been observed several nights in a row, in the direction indicated by all the witnesses, disappearing behind the horizon. All of these individuals had been observing Venus.

summary: Close observation of the movement of a cylindrical object flying 10m above the ground with a change of direction.
description: On November 25, 1976, at approximately 7:10 a.m., a farmer out hunting observed a red glow in the distance for a few seconds, which he mistook for a chimney fire. Overlooking the landscape, he then saw a shimmering light approaching him, moving along an east-west trajectory. When the object was ten to fifteen meters from the hunter, it changed direction, and the witness realized he was in the presence of an elongated object approximately two meters long. The cylindrical object was stationary ten meters above the ground, and an intermittent red glow spread around it. It then moved silently southward, stopped, then moved off again and disappeared, hidden by the landscape. Following the police investigation, no other witness statements were collected, and no trace was found in the area indicated by the witness. It is difficult to conduct a retrospective investigation into such an old case. The hypothesis of an aircraft sighting is ruled out. This unexplained case is inconsistent (a single witness). The sighting exhibits a high degree of strangeness (close but brief observation, 8 to 10 seconds). In the current GEIPAN classification, this inconsistent unexplained case with a high degree of strangeness is classified as UAP D1.

summary: Observing the movement of a point of light in the sky.
description: On November 21, 1976, at 8:55 PM, a person observed a red streak in the sky, followed by its disappearance. This person and another witness then saw a white point of light move along a curved, downward trajectory. No further accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a luminous object in the sky.
description: On November 20, 1976, at approximately 7:30 PM, several people observed a round, luminous object in the sky, which intrigued them. This object appeared to rotate, and a glow was visible intermittently. It emitted bright yellow-orange beams. The observation lasted for about fifteen minutes before the object disappeared in a downward trajectory. No further, more precise accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observations of the slow movement of two bright points in the sky.
description: On November 20th and 21st, 1976, at approximately 5:30 PM, several people observed the slow movement of two luminous points in the sky. They were round in shape. No sound was heard during the observations. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Periodic observations of the presence of an unusual object in the sky by a single witness.
description: On November 11, 12, and 20, 1977, between 5:30 p.m. and 6:45 p.m., a witness observed an unusual object in the sky that intrigued him. Triangular in shape and varying in color, the object appeared to be either stationary or moving. No other witness statements were collected. The gendarmerie made no further observations regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On November 5, 1976, at 5:00 PM and 8:08 PM, people observed an intense white glow across the sky. This circular phenomenon moved rapidly along a northeast trajectory. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted a few seconds. Too few details were provided to confirm any particular hypothesis. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Probable observation of an aircraft passing overhead.
description: On November 4, 1976, at approximately 9:45 PM, several witnesses observed the slow and silent passage of a triangular shape following the Marseille-La Ciotat route. The object was slightly larger than a passenger plane and emitted a red light from the front and a white glow from the rear. During several night shifts, the gendarmerie observed, between approximately 9:30 PM and 10:00 PM, the passage of a fairly large passenger plane following the same route as the observed object. The witnesses likely saw an aircraft.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: During the night of October 28-29, 1976, between 4:00 and 4:45 AM, several people witnessed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. A stationary, circular object emitted a very intense white light. Few details were given regarding the object's possible altitude. These individuals were likely making an astronomical observation.

summary: Successive observations of lights coming from an aircraft.
description: Between the evenings of October 20th and 26th, 1976, several people in the same geographical area observed multicolored lights that appeared to be coming from an unidentified craft. The witnesses were frightened by the lights and the craft, which was either stationary or moving and emitting a muffled noise. This phenomenon was classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of two luminous phenomena.
description: On October 21, 1976, between 6:30 and 6:45 PM, three people in two different locations observed a bright, reddish-orange sphere moving slowly from southeast to northwest. The observation lasted 45 seconds before the phenomenon abruptly disappeared. A second phenomenon, identical to the first and seemingly following the same trajectory, was seen a few minutes later. This phenomenon is classified as category C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a craft emitting lights towards the ground.
description: On October 19, 1976, at approximately 11:40 PM, a family in a car observed a peculiar object in the sky, equipped with beams of light at each end. This object emitted lights towards the ground, then rose after its beams were switched off and disappeared to the east. A resident of the valley where the observation took place noticed disturbances on their television around 11:30 PM but made no direct observation. No information to validate a hypothesis was gathered from the various contacted services (weather service, radar service, EDF, wastewater treatment and rendering plants located nearby and operating day and night).

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: A witness briefly reported observing a luminous object moving across the sky on October 15, 1976, at approximately 5:55 PM, following a south-south trajectory. It then appeared as a large cigar-shaped object, still moving silently. The object disappeared, heading northeast. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Probable sighting of a passing airship.
description: On October 10, 1976, between 5:00 and 5:30 PM, several people observed a bright, cigar-shaped object with a dark circle in its center. This object moved silently. No other reports were received. These witnesses likely observed a dirigible-type aircraft used for advertising.

summary: Probable observation of an aircraft passing overhead.
description: On October 7, 1976, several teenagers observed, for a few seconds around 7:00 PM, an object rapidly passing over the houses in the neighborhood. The object was described as being shaped like a red cigar and passing silently along a southeast-northwest trajectory. No adults witnessed this phenomenon, which was reported in the local press at the insistence of one of the parents. These children likely observed an aircraft, as air traffic was significant in this area located near Metz Airport.

summary: Successive observations of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On October 5th and 6th, 1976, between 6:30 and 6:40 AM, two witnesses observed a bright point in the sky that intrigued them. A luminous, oval-shaped object, bright red in color, appeared stationary to the north during the first observation and moving slowly east-west during the second. The object's presence lasted less than a minute before the phenomenon suddenly disappeared. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we have little information.

summary: Observation of the passage of a CNES stratospheric balloon.
description: On September 17, 1976, between 8:15 and 8:30 PM, several people observed the silent movement of a luminous, spherical object. Some witnesses noted changes in color. The police investigation quickly determined that it was a stratospheric balloon belonging to the National Center for Space Studies (CNES), which had landed at Aire-sur-l'Adour (40) to conduct high-altitude measurements. The color changes were caused by the diffraction of light from the setting sun, while atmospheric movements distorted the object's contours.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon and sensation of intense heat during stormy weather. Sudden disappearance. Probable observation of a ball lightning phenomenon.
description: On September 12, 1976, at approximately 10:50 PM, a family observed a luminous phenomenon near their home. On the doorstep, one of the witnesses felt intense heat around their house and their attention was drawn to an elliptical shape of incandescent white with a luminous halo. This phenomenon, located behind some trees, lasted about two minutes and descended towards the ground. It disappeared abruptly. Moments earlier, a disturbance had been observed on the television screen, and an animal had been suddenly startled. The following day, the police found no trace of the phenomenon on the ground in the area where it was observed. A neighbor reported hearing what sounded like thunder around 11:00 PM and noting a power outage for a few minutes, but he did not see the phenomenon. This case was classified as a Category C observation for a long time due to a lack of information. It was recently submitted to a lightning expert. The atmospheric conditions at the time of observation and the description of the phenomenon's behavior are consistent with the hypothesis of a manifestation of atmospheric electricity known as ball lightning or globular lightning. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of a globular lightning phenomenon.

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: On September 10, 1976, at 11:15 PM, a witness observed a round object, about the size of a helicopter, passing in a northwest-east direction. It rapidly emitted three colors: yellow, green, and red. No sound was heard during the 45-second observation. The witness later reported the sighting to the gendarmerie. No other witness statements were collected, despite a press article about the event. The witness likely observed an aircraft.

summary: Probable sighting of a weather balloon.
description: On September 5, 1976, at approximately 7:22 a.m., a person on the 15th floor of their building observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the sky. For about ten minutes, the witness observed a red line of light in the southeast, above the hills of Sarrouilles (65), before it disappeared to the east. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The police investigation revealed that the observation made on September 5 was probably directly related to the passage of a weather balloon that remained aloft after its payload was released in a field in Soues. There were no winds on September 4 and 5, 1976, and both towns are located in roughly the same direction southeast of Tarbes.

summary: Observing the passage of a luminous phenomenon across the sky.
description: On August 28, 1976, at approximately 4:30 a.m., a witness observed a luminous phenomenon in the overcast sky. A bright red sphere at its center passed quickly and silently overhead and disappeared, hidden by the landscape. The witness's dog was frightened. The witness then saw a white, semi-circular glow, motionless behind a curtain of trees in the direction the phenomenon had vanished. No trace of the object was found at the site, and no further accounts of this phenomenon were reported, leaving us with little information.

summary: Probable observations of the passage of an aircraft.
description: On August 27, 1976, at approximately 9:16 PM, an amateur astronomer once again observed an intriguing object in the cloudy sky. He reported to another person the passage of a circular craft emitting a distinctly orange light from its rear. During the investigation, the witness provided a precise description, a diagram of the observed object, and its trajectory. No other witness statements were collected. It is likely that this witness had made several observations of an aircraft.

summary: Probable observation of the passage of a helicopter type aircraft.
description: On August 23, 1976, at approximately 11:30 PM, a moped rider observed a bright red object moving southwest in the sky. Upon arriving home, intrigued by a high-pitched electric motor sound, he went outside and saw, about 15 meters away, a luminous, ovoid object with white and red lights moving northwest. The witness noted that after traveling 80 meters, the object stabilized and then rapidly ascended at a very high speed before disappearing. During the police investigation, no other reports of this phenomenon were received that evening. However, the witness stated that, finishing work late, he had repeatedly witnessed the movement of light sources. Furthermore, the local press reported various observations in June and August 1976 that could be related to this phenomenon. The observation presented a low degree of strangeness. A large proportion of the characteristics described by the witness correspond to those of known phenomena: in this case, a helicopter. The observation is explainable, and the proposed interpretation is simply plausible. The case is not very strange and does not warrant a thorough investigation (identifying the helicopter flight involved would, moreover, be difficult for such an old case). The testimony is unique, and the case has little substance. Due to the strong resemblance to the appearance of a helicopter, the case is classified as B, indicating a probable helicopter sighting.

summary: Observation of an advertising balloon.
description: On August 3, 1976, at approximately 11:45 a.m., a farmer observed a cylindrical, aluminum-colored object moving slowly in the sky and shining continuously. The observation lasted 30 minutes before the object disappeared over the horizon. During a neighborhood inquiry, several people identified the object based on the description, identifying it as an advertising balloon for a tire manufacturer, which had been seen several times that same day.

summary: Observation of a spherical object hovering in flight then disappearing towards the East.
description: On July 30, 1976, at approximately 2:51 PM, a witness was intrigued by a spherical, metallic-colored object that remained stationary in the sky. No unusual noises were heard during the observation, which lasted three minutes before the object disappeared to the east. No further reports were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observations of different light phenomena.
description: Between July 26 and July 29, 1976, at different times, several witnesses observed luminous and electrical phenomena that intrigued them. One witness observed the rapid passage of a flashing green ball across the sky, leaving a red trail. Disruptions to television reception and an electrical meter fire were also reported during this period. The gendarmerie investigation gathered several testimonies of different observations. This case was classified as C due to a lack of coherence and information in the testimonies.

summary: Observations of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: Three people from the same area observed a luminous phenomenon on the night of July 23-24, 1976, around midnight. A bright, bluish-white light moved silently at low altitude. It disappeared in a southeasterly direction. The police investigation, including interviews with a farmer who witnessed the event, failed to uncover any trace or clue suggesting the low-altitude passage of any aircraft or object. The vegetation in the area indicated by the main witness remained untouched, and no anomalies from a heat source or air movement were observed. The descriptions are insufficient, and this phenomenon is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a stationary green luminous phenomenon and disappearance towards the NE.
description: On July 19, 1976, at approximately 3:00 AM, a motorist observed a stationary object of intense green color and brightness for a few seconds. The observation distance was approximately 300 to 400 meters. The object's shape reminded him of a bowler hat. The witness heard no unusual noise when a reddish color appeared at the rear of the object and it quickly disappeared to the northeast. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Probable observation of an aircraft passing overhead.
description: On the night of July 16, 1976, at 4:30 a.m., a witness observed a luminous phenomenon from a window of his home. He could not clearly see any shape or hear any particular noise. He described his observation as initially seeing a point of light approaching and becoming a beam of lights, before finally, from behind, seeing two points of light, one green and one red. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, which was likely an aircraft sighting.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon vertically above a TV relay.
description: On July 15, 1976, around midnight, several people observed a multi-colored luminous phenomenon on Mount "Malgré Tout," where a TV relay station was located. The phenomenon moved rapidly, but no sound was heard during the 20 minutes of observation. Despite a police investigation and observations made with binoculars by witnesses, we lack information and details about this observed phenomenon.

summary: Probable observation of a phenomenon of reflection of the rising sun.
description: On July 13, 1976, at 5:45 a.m., two witnesses finishing their night shift at a quarry suddenly observed a stationary white sphere in the sky, which gradually grew larger. The observation lasted four to five seconds, then the phenomenon disappeared. No sound was heard. According to the police investigation, the observers were in the highest point in the region and had a very wide field of vision. The weather was sunny and cloudless. The phenomenon was located directly above the Vaucouleurs ridge at a distance of approximately 8 kilometers. At that time and date, it is likely that these individuals witnessed a reflection of the sun just after it had risen.

summary: Observing the movement of a luminous phenomenon lacks information.
description: On July 11, 1976, at approximately 10:05 PM, two people observed a stationary, circular, bright red luminous phenomenon. The distant observation (approximately 2 km) did not allow for any discernible details. While one of the witnesses searched for his binoculars, the phenomenon moved westward and then disappeared. No other witness statements were collected. The gendarmerie investigation, which took place at the scene with the witnesses, determined the presence of a 50-meter-long dirt track that connects to an unclassified and unidentified local road to the west. The possibility of a passing vehicle was considered. However, given the distance of observation and the limited details provided, no evidence allowed for the identification of the phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a flying object following the road.
description: On July 10, 1976, at approximately 4:30 a.m., a motorist noticed an unfamiliar object hovering low above the road in front of him. The witness described an object approximately 4 to 5 meters long and 1 meter in diameter. Bright red in color, it had a black band running its entire length. The upper part appeared to be topped with a cabin containing a flashing light. The motorist stopped to look at the object, which seemed to be moving backward, as if approaching him. Frightened, the driver immediately continued driving. No further information was gathered by the police.

summary: Observation in the mountains of circular tracks on the ground.
description: On July 9, 1976, a game warden was alerted by a shepherd to the presence of tracks on the ground that the latter had observed on June 25, 1976. On July 26, 1976, the gendarmerie investigation confirmed the presence of circular tracks in the determined area, but the origin of these old tracks could not be defined.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous green ball.
description: A witness and his grandson observed a bright, green, spherical object passing north-south for about a minute at approximately 7:20 PM. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and we lack further information.

summary: Observation of the passage of three luminous spheres.
description: On July 2, 1976, at approximately 10:15 PM, a couple observed three luminous orbs passing west-northeast from a distance of 500 meters for a few seconds. They quickly disappeared over the horizon. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena corresponding to the headlights of a vehicle.
description: witness reported seeing several luminous phenomena at night, accompanied by the sound of an engine. The police investigation concluded that a vehicle had passed near the witness's farm.

summary: Observation of a red glow passing at high altitude.
description: On June 22, 1976, at approximately 10:15 PM, several people in cars observed a red glow moving quickly and silently high in the sky, which intrigued them. This stationary phenomenon, initially above the oil terminal, reportedly passed over the Herrlisheim-Drusenheim refinery and then headed towards the Rhine River and Germany. One of the witnesses took several photographs, but the film proved unusable. Two refinery employees reported seeing a bright object from their homes in the east-northeast direction indicated by the first witness, but none of the refinery's security guards saw anything above the facility. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Sighting of a cigar-shaped object.
description: On June 18, 1976, at approximately 9:30 PM, two people observed a luminous object in the sky that intrigued them: it was cigar-shaped and quite long. This object flew at a low altitude and at a steady speed along a northeast-southwest trajectory. No sound was heard. Only one eyewitness account was collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack further information.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On June 6, 1976, at approximately 11:35 PM, a motorist observed a luminous phenomenon descending at a constant speed and then exploding for a few seconds. No sound was heard. Thinking it might be an aircraft accident, the witness informed the police. The investigation revealed that no aircraft had been reported missing. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon. The motorist likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of a stratospheric balloon and its flight chain.
description: On June 6, 1976, between 5:40 and 7:20 a.m., a witness observed a luminous, ovoid object moving at high altitude. The object appeared to be composed of two luminous parts of unequal size, seemingly connected. It moved slowly in an east-west direction. No other reports were collected. This person likely witnessed the passage of a stratospheric balloon.

summary: Probable observation of aircraft evolutions.
description: On May 24, 1976, two witnesses observed a bright, elongated object moving back and forth in the sky, leaving no trace. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted two or three minutes. These witnesses likely observed the maneuvers of an aircraft on a training exercise, but their account remains very vague.

summary: Observation of the passage of two luminous red balls.
description: During the night of May 18-19, 1976, around 2:00 AM, a witness observed two red, conical spheres passing northeast. No traces were found on the ground near the home of the sole witness to the phenomenon. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Probable observation of an electromagnetic phenomenon due to a climatic event.
description: Alerted by newspaper articles in the local press, the gendarmerie investigated a peculiar phenomenon observed by several people. On April 24, 1976, around 4:00 PM, a couple in the countryside noticed the unusual sound of a strong gust of air followed by the appearance, 300 meters away, of two luminous green discs. These objects suddenly plunged rapidly toward the ground before disappearing. A violent gust of wind followed by a snowfall occurred. The same phenomenon was repeated two more times. In the vicinity, other people noticed disturbances on their television sets at the same time. Information from the local brigade suggested that it was probably an electromagnetic phenomenon caused by a local meteorological event.

summary: Observation of a stationary orange luminous phenomenon. Sudden disappearance.
description: On April 15, 1976, between 9:00 and 9:30 PM, a witness observed an orange light phenomenon for approximately two minutes. It remained stationary above the steeple of a church located two kilometers away. No unusual noise was heard. It disappeared suddenly. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena.
description: On June 19, 1976, a witness reported three sightings of luminous phenomena between April and June 1976. On April 7, 1976, around 11:30 p.m., he noticed a cigar-shaped luminous object in the sky. This object landed on the path leading to his home and emitted a bright light directed in a single direction. During May 1976, around the same time and practically in the same location, he noticed two very bright objects, one of which appeared to land on the path near his home. Immediately waking his brother and parents, they observed these luminous phenomena for about an hour and a half without being able to determine a precise shape. No sound was heard. Everything disappeared abruptly. One of the witnesses later found traces on the asphalt of the road at the presumed landing site. On Friday, June 16th, at the same time, the witness noticed a bright light on a field near his home. Following these observations, he decided to give his statement. During the police investigation, no findings could be made regarding the first two observations due to the witness's late declaration. As for the third observation, the landowner stated that he had lit a wood fire in his field that evening for a barbecue.

summary: A firecracker exploded, producing smoke and leaving traces on the ground.
description: On April 8, 1976, the gendarmerie was alerted by the press that on April 5, 1976, around 9:00 PM, a person had observed a UFO near a sports field. At the precise location of the sighting, several traces of burnt grass were found, and the charred stump of a tree was discovered. During his statement, the witness said he saw a light that alternated between white and red after a puff of smoke. He described the dimensions of an aluminum-colored object that was hovering over the stream. The witness heard a faint whistling sound. The sighting lasted five minutes. The gendarmerie investigation determined that the traces were caused by firecrackers set off by several people. The witness admitted that he had never seen any craft and that journalists had given him the dimensions of the object he thought he had seen.

summary: Probable observation of an object falling into the sea.
description: On April 1, 1976, at approximately 5:20 PM, several people observed a white trail in the sky that appeared to plunge into the sea. They then saw a mass of gray smoke that lingered on the water for about fifteen minutes before disappearing completely. According to the gendarmerie investigation, no aircraft from the airport were in flight after 5:00 PM. No objects or debris of any kind were recovered from the shoreline. It is likely that the witnesses saw an object fall into the sea, but we lack the information to identify it.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a circular orange object.
description: On March 29, 1976, at 5:10 PM, a witness observed and photographed a circular, orange object flying in the sky. The object moved slowly, paused briefly, and then accelerated to a north-south trajectory. No sound was heard during the object's movement. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a phenomenon in the form of a fog bank.
description: On March 27, 1976, between 6:30 and 6:55 a.m., a soldier in his vehicle suddenly broke down. All the warning lights were out. His attention was then drawn to a patch of grayish fog with a metallic sheen. It was located near the river, 15 or 20 meters from the vehicle. Looking out the window, he watched the phenomenon rise and disappear at high speed above the buildings in a south-southwest direction. Very surprised by what he had just seen, he noticed that his dashboard lights were on and easily restarted the engine to drive off. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a luminous, oval-shaped flying object surmounted by a deme.
description: On March 25, 1976, at approximately 2:30 PM, a motorist and his passengers observed a luminous object moving east-west in the sky. Large and oval-shaped, topped with a dome, it remained in their field of vision for about a minute before suddenly disappearing. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. This case is classified as D1 (see investigation report).

summary: Observation of two semi-buried hemispheres on a beach.
description: On March 24, 1976, a restaurant manager notified the gendarmerie that two brightly colored spheres, approximately one meter in diameter, had just been discovered on the beach at La Feuillère (Marie-Galante Island, Guadeloupe). The gendarmerie confirmed the two spheres were indeed buried in the sand at the edge of the breaking wave and partially submerged by seawater. They were 14 meters apart. A thin metallic coating (approximately 0.5 millimeters thick) covered both spheres; on one of them, the coating appeared to have melted, revealing a harder, more resistant metal that could not be scratched with a knife. The following day at 6:30 a.m., the objects were removed by the gendarmerie, and it appeared that they were two hemispheres belonging to the same craft, fitting perfectly inside one another. The inscription "H 476 AC" was legible on one of the hemispheres. These craft were to be taken to the brigade for cleaning and possible identification. However, at 10:00 a.m. that same day, the mayor of Capesterre de Marie-Galante, despite the gendarmerie's prohibition, had the hemispheres removed and displayed in the town square. This case is not a UFO sighting. It concerns the recovery of two metallic hemispheres on a beach. The origin of these hemispheres might perhaps be traced using the markings found inside one of them.

summary: Quick observation of the movement of a red sphere.
description: On February 27, 1976 (the exact date is unclear in the police report), at approximately 8:50 PM, a motorist observed, for a few seconds and at low altitude, the very rapid movement of a very bright red sphere from north to south. Several people in the area, when questioned, stated that they had noticed nothing unusual that evening. This case is classified as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observations of a moving luminous mass: astronomical observations linked with a misinterpretation of the Moon.
description: On February 9, 1976, at 2:05 a.m., a motorist and his passengers were intrigued and then frightened by the presence of a luminous mass in the slightly overcast sky. Their observation began at the Lueon exit (85). They then parked their vehicle at the Beugne-L'Abbe exit (in the commune of Les Magnils-Reigniers (85)) but remained inside, observing the luminous phenomenon for two to three minutes. They described the shape as two shallow bowls, one on top of the other, each about twenty meters in diameter. Initially stationary at treetop level, this mass then slowly gained altitude. No unusual noise was heard during the observation. The witnesses then resumed their journey towards Les Sables-d'Olonne (85) and were still able to visually follow the phenomenon and see it disappear to the west. The gendarmerie, notified immediately, found no trace in the indicated area. No other reports concerning the observation of a particular phenomenon at that time were collected. No electrical disturbances on the network in the area were recorded by EDF (the French electricity company). Another witness reported seeing two silent and unusual objects pass in the sky on Sunday, February 8, 1976, at 8:00 PM. This case is consistent (3 witnesses), and the description of the observation site and the observed UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) is precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, color, size, etc.) with a known astronomical phenomenon: the Moon. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed in the area of the sky observed, even though the witnesses did not mention it. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observations through their feelings (fatigue, anxiety, fear, and belief in the UFO phenomenon). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case, described as having low strangeness, is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the Moon.

summary: Observation of a flying object, no noise.
description: On February 5, 1976, at 12:45 a.m., two people observed a stationary flying object within a luminous cluster. The witnesses placed it 25 meters from the house and 15 meters above the ground. Two figures were seen inside the craft, which then disappeared slowly in a south-southeast direction without any sound being heard. The gendarmerie found no evidence in the area indicated, and no other witness statements were collected.

summary: Observation of a glow preceded by a double "bang".
description: On February 3, 1976, at approximately 7:30 PM, several witnesses observed a silvery-white glow in the sky. After rising above the hill, the glow gradually disappeared on the hidden slope. This phenomenon was preceded by a noise similar to that of a supersonic aircraft. The gendarmerie ruled out the possibility of a fire or a body falling, as no traces were found on the ground in the area. The case was classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Brief observation of the dazzling passage of an emerald-green object across the sky.
description: On January 13, 1976, at 5:50 PM, a witness was astonished by what he saw in the sky. A luminous, circular, emerald-green shape, adorned with a copper-red halo, passed overhead. Its trajectory was straight, from west to east. No sound was heard. It disappeared very quickly, hidden by the landscape and then over the horizon. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Probable sighting of the star Sirius.
description: On January 24, 1976, several people, including police officers, observed a distant, luminous object in the sky between 7:40 p.m. and 10:30 p.m., emitting green and orange glows. This object moved noticeably. No sound was heard. All these witnesses were likely observing the star Sirius, which was particularly visible at that time of year.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous circular object.
description: On January 19, 1976, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness leaving his home observed a disc-shaped object, 2.5 meters in diameter and phosphorescent orange in color, for three minutes. It appeared to be resting on a paved road along a ridge. The witness saw the object move at a low altitude in the valley before disappearing behind some farm buildings. No unusual noises were heard during the object's movement. Neither the witness nor his son found any particular traces at the presumed location of the object. Two other people reported seeing a peculiar light that evening on the road, but their accounts were all very brief. The case is classified as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the slow passage of an unknown craft.
description: On January 17, 1976, around 6:00 PM, a farmer observed an unfamiliar vehicle passing over the woods. It moved slowly from east to west without making any noise. During the one-minute observation, the witness noticed a powerful spotlight illuminate the field. The witness went to fetch his son, but by the time they returned, the vehicle had disappeared. Despite a police investigation, no further witness statements or information were gathered.

summary: Observations of the slow passage of a red object at high altitude.
description: On January 13, 1976, around 11:00 PM, a witness observed a red, elongated object moving through binoculars. No sound was heard, and the object gradually disappeared. This witness made the same observation on January 15 at the same time. The gendarmerie made similar observations on January 17 and 18 between 10:50 PM and 11:30 PM, following a SSE-NNW trajectory. The descriptions gathered are similar to those of satellite sightings, but we lack sufficient data to confirm this hypothesis.

summary: Probable sighting of a weather balloon at sunrise.
description: On January 10, 1976, between 7:50 and 8:50 a.m., two people observed a very bright, spherical object above the horizon. The witnesses noted that this object remained stationary. It gradually ceased to be visible with sunrise. The gendarmerie, contacted quickly, found no object in the sky that morning or the following morning. No other reports were collected. Based on the descriptions gathered, the witnesses likely observed a weather balloon.

summary: Probable observation of the movement of a ball.
description: On January 9, 1976, at 7:50 a.m., a motorist and his wife observed a bright object moving in the sky. This object, shaped like a balloon with a truncated top, moved slowly and horizontally along a sea-to-mountain trajectory, following the contours of the land. It disappeared into the landscape. No other reports were collected. Based on the description given, these witnesses likely observed the movement of a balloon at sunrise.

summary: Various accounts of sightings of luminous objects following a press article: lack of information.
description: Following an article published in the local press (not present in the GEIPAN archives), several people gave statements to the gendarmerie regarding their observations made during January 1976 (the 5th is indicated for the first observation). Each witness observed a particular luminous phenomenon or object on different days, at different times, and in different locations. One witness said he saw a man emerge from a device placed on the ground and walk towards him. Frightened, the witness fled. He said he had the same encounter the next day. The gendarmerie found no trace or clue at the scene to confirm or refute the brief statements of the witnesses.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On January 1, 1976, at approximately 7:45 PM, several people on public transportation observed a luminous phenomenon crossing the sky. In the darkness, a circular shape bathed in a bright glow rapidly traversed the sky along a northeast-southwest trajectory. No sound was heard during the rapid passage of this phenomenon, about which we lack information.
